correctness.rationale: The defining equation implies \(\sigma(p^{a-1})\sigma(q^{b-1})=p^a q^b\). Each geometric sum is \(1\) modulo its own base prime. Equal base primes are therefore impossible; for distinct primes the support identity forces the sums to be \(q^b\) and \(p^a\). The exponent-one boundaries are impossible by the same support argument, and substitution for \(a,b\ge2\) yields \((p-1)(q-1)p^{a-1}=p^{a-1}-1\), an immediate contradiction.

value.rationale: Prime powers are the minimal multiplicative support class for the divisor-sum function. The theorem gives a sharp, uniform boundary for harmonious pairs: both members cannot simultaneously have one-prime support. This is a complete all-prime, all-exponent structural result rather than a finite computation.
